title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 25 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 25)

content.overview: Section 25 distinguishes the consequences of claimant and respondent default. Failure by the claimant to communicate the statement of claim leads to termination of proceedings. Failure by the respondent to communicate a defence does not amount to admission, and the tribunal may continue. Failure to appear or produce evidence permits the tribunal to continue and make the award on the evidence before it.

content.study:
Section 25 — Default of a party

Section 25 distinguishes the consequences of claimant and respondent default. Failure by the claimant to communicate the statement of claim leads to termination of proceedings. Failure by the respondent to communicate a defence does not amount to admission, and the tribunal may continue. Failure to appear or produce evidence permits the tribunal to continue and make the award on the evidence before it.
